summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with a history of transfusion-dependent anemia, likely due to myelodysplastic syndrome, chronic abdominal pain, and long-term anticoagulation presented with worsening left upper quadrant pain. Her hemoglobin was 6.1 g/dL, consistent with her usual pattern of symptomatic anemia. She received one unit of packed red blood cells, after which her hemoglobin improved to 9.4 g/dL and her pain decreased. Her INR was elevated at 4.2, so warfarin was held for two days and restarted at a reduced dose. Guaiac-positive stool suggested possible gastrointestinal bleeding, but no overt melena was observed. The patient declined further GI evaluation. Omeprazole was increased to 40 mg daily to reduce gastric injury risk. Chronic lung findings were stable on chest X-ray. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for hematology and INR monitoring.
problems: Anemia in other chronic diseases classified elsewhere
